facts.text: Corinthia Rome is a grand palazzo on Piazza del Parlamento in Rome's historic heart.
facts.excerpt: In Rome’s historic heart, Corinthia Rome opens the doors of a grand palazzo on Piazza del Parlamento.

facts.text: The palazzo was long associated with the Bank of Italy.
facts.excerpt: Long associated as a stronghold of the Bank of Italy, the landmark is reborn as a noble Roman residence

facts.text: The hotel is in the historic Campo Marzio district.
facts.excerpt: Located on Piazza del Parlamento in the heart of the historic Campo Marzio district

facts.text: The Corinthia Spa occupies the bank's former historic vault beneath the hotel.
facts.excerpt: Once the bank’s historic vault, the space now protects something far more precious: time for yourself.

facts.text: The spa is inspired by the ritual of Roman bathing and shaped by water, mineral stone and softened light.
facts.excerpt: Inspired by the ritual of Roman bathing, the Corinthia Spa unfolds as an intimate subterranean retreat shaped by water, mineral stone and softened light

facts.text: The spa has a tepidarium, calidarium and frigidarium.
facts.excerpt: There’s a tepidarium, calidarium, and frigidarium

facts.text: A spa path leads from two baths at different temperatures to a hammam, sauna, ice fountain and heated black-stone beds.
facts.excerpt: a path leads from two baths at different temperatures to a hammam, sauna, ice fountain, and then beds of heated black stones where you can recline and relax

facts.text: Spa treatments use Seed to Skin, an Italian brand with natural Tuscan botanicals, and 111Skin.
facts.excerpt: the Italian brand Seed to Skin, which uses natural Tuscan botanicals, and the anti-aging line 111Skin

facts.text: Dining at the hotel is curated by chef Carlo Cracco, in his Roman debut.
facts.excerpt: curated by Italy’s celebrated chef Carlo Cracco in his Roman debut

facts.text: Viride is the hotel's fine-dining restaurant by Michelin-starred chef Carlo Cracco.
facts.excerpt: At Viride, Michelin-starred chef Carlo Cracco reimagines Italian gastronomy

facts.text: Piazzetta is a lively open-kitchen and garden retreat at the heart of the palazzo.
facts.excerpt: Piazzetta is the heart of the palazzo. A lively open-kitchen and garden retreat

facts.text: The Sala del Consiglio on the piano nobile has frescoes by Giulio Bargellini on the theme of prosperity.
facts.excerpt: The centerpiece is the Sala del Consiglio on the piano nobile, with frescoes by Giulio Bargellini on the theme of prosperity.

facts.text: Restoration uncovered mosaics, stuccoes, cornices, painted ceilings and marble details.
facts.excerpt: The project uncovered exquisite mosaics, stuccoes, cornices, painted ceilings, and marble details.

facts.text: Rooms have high ceilings and large windows, with views of the city's rooftops or the quiet inner courtyard.
facts.excerpt: Soffitti alti e grandi finestre lasciano entrare la luce naturale, con viste sui tetti della città o sul tranquillo cortile interno.

facts.text: The Chigi Suite opens onto a large panoramic rooftop terrace.
facts.excerpt: la Chigi Suite si apre su un’ampia terrazza panoramica sul tetto

facts.text: The Campo Marzio Suites are on two levels.
facts.excerpt: Le Campo Marzio Suites si sviluppano su due livelli

facts.text: The Theodoli Heritage Suite incorporates the Sala del Consiglio, where the bank's board met, as its living room.
facts.excerpt: the Theodoli Heritage Suite, on the first floor, incorporates the Sala de Consiglio, where the bank’s board of directors would meet, as its living room

facts.text: From the Arte Suite you can see the Vatican.
facts.excerpt: From the Arte Suite, you can see the Vatican

facts.text: Rooms have marble bathrooms and plenty of space and light.
facts.excerpt: lots of space, plenty of light, and marble bathrooms

facts.text: All rooms include books on art, culture and history.
facts.excerpt: lots of books on art, culture, and history

facts.text: The hotel faces Palazzo Montecitorio, the seat of the Italian parliament, near Via del Corso.
facts.excerpt: facing the Palazzo Montecitorio, the seat of the Italian parliament, and near the Via del Corso

facts.text: Corinthia Rome is the first Italian property from Corinthia.
facts.excerpt: the first Italian property from Corinthia

facts.text: There are four guestrooms designed for guests with mobility, hearing or visual impairments.
facts.excerpt: There are four guestrooms specifically designed for those with mobility, hearing, or visual impairments.

facts.text: The 1920s building served as the offices of the Bank of Italy until 1961.
facts.excerpt: Until 1961, the 1920s building served as the offices of the Bank of Italy.

facts.text: The listed nature of the building presents some accessibility challenges in public areas.
facts.excerpt: the listed nature of the building presents some challenges

facts.text: The hotel is moments from the Pantheon, Trevi Fountain and Spanish Steps.
facts.excerpt: just moments from the Pantheon, Trevi Fountain and Spanish Steps

facts.text: Ocra is the hotel's bar, with signature cocktails and rare vintages.
facts.excerpt: Fine spirits meet the artistry of mixology, with signature cocktails and rare vintages

facts.text: Corinthia Rome was named to Conde Nast Traveler's Hot List 2026.
facts.excerpt: Hot List 2026

facts.text: The palace has an austere and elegant facade, generous spaces, high ceilings and beautiful terraces.
facts.excerpt: The palace—with its austere and elegant façade, generous spaces, high ceilings, and beautiful terraces—has been effectively preserved.
